unit: Guest instructions per operation under icount, log scale
title: What Each Kernel Operation Costs
subtitle: QEMU virt with -icount shift=0, where one virtual nanosecond is one guest instruction

rows.label: swtch, one direction
rows.detail: Raw context switch, 14 registers saved and 14 loaded. TCG wall clock 50 to 52 ns over three runs

rows.label: Trap round trip, ebreak
rows.detail: Into kernelvec, full 304-byte frame, kernel_trap and sret. TCG wall clock 1158 to 1225 ns

rows.label: yield, scheduler switch
rows.detail: Thread to thread, including sched_lock, the run queue and bookkeeping. TCG wall clock 570 to 601 ns

rows.label: SBI ecall round trip
rows.detail: S-mode to OpenSBI in M-mode and back. TCG wall clock 1520 to 1583 ns

rows.label: pmm_free
rows.detail: Bitmap free with alignment, range and double-free checks. TCG wall clock 354 to 374 ns

rows.label: kmalloc(64) plus kfree
rows.detail: One pair. TCG wall clock 850 to 868 ns

rows.label: pmm_alloc, zeroing 4 KiB
rows.detail: TCG wall clock 1622 to 1645 ns, less than the instruction count because QEMU runs the store loop faster than one instruction per nanosecond

caption: Instruction counts are deterministic and were identical across two icount runs. They are QEMU guest instructions, not cycles on real RISC-V hardware. TCG wall clock ranges in the tooltips were measured on a Mac with a load average of 129 to 151 from other jobs.
